rules.question: What does a command-line tool do when hydra_rules.ini is bad?

exempt.why: The app answers a different question on purpose: it keeps running with analysis off (AppState::rules_error) instead of exiting.

must_not_match: if (const int code = hydra::app::load_tool_rules(rulespath, settings.rules)) return code;
rules.note: Four tools (hydra_batch, hydra_fillcompare, hydra_bench, hydra_replay) each caught the loader's error and printed it on their own. They call load_tool_rules now, so a fifth tool that catches it itself is flagged. Found by: concept audit M25.

rules.question: What does the user read when hydra_rules.ini is bad?
rules.owner: kAnalysisOffSentence and rules_file_tool_text in src/app/user_messages.h and .cpp
must_match: static constexpr const char* kAnalysisOffSentence = "hydra_rules.ini has an error, so analysis is off";
constexpr const char* kRulesFile = "hydra_rules.ini has a line Hydra can't read.";
rules.note: One state, a bad hydra_rules.ini, once had three wordings: the app's (on AppState), a dead kRulesFile sentence, and the tools' raw line. The app's sentence and the tools' lead-in both live in user_messages now. Decided by: D114 item 11, concept audit M72.
